findings.reason: The central identification of the coincidence locus with a diagonal preimage has a concrete four-object pullback square. Displaying that square materially clarifies the domains, codomains and common coincidence set without attempting to encode the orientation signs. Original standalone tiles show no such diagram.
findings.action: Added a labeled tikzcd pullback square and definitions of j and h in a final Remarks section.

correction: Added an explanatory pullback square X×_M Z → Δ_M over X×Z → M×M, with defined maps and an explicit proof-independence sentence.

diagram_math_checks.justification: The original Statement, F1 and proof step 1.1 define X×_M Z as {(a,b):f(a)=g(b)}=(f×g)^−1(Δ_M). F2 identifies Δ_M as the diagonal submanifold.

diagram_math_checks.maps: j:X×_M Z→X×Z; h:X×_M Z→Δ_M; i_Δ:Δ_M→M×M; f×g:X×Z→M×M
diagram_math_checks.justification: j and i_Δ are inclusions. h(a,b)=(f(a),g(b)) lies in Δ_M precisely because f(a)=g(b); it is the restriction/corestriction of the product map. Thus all four arrow domains and codomains match their nodes.

diagram_math_checks.relation: i_Δ∘h=(f×g)∘j; the square is a pullback
diagram_math_checks.justification: Both paths send (a,b) to (f(a),g(b)). For any point of X×Z whose product image lies in Δ_M, f(a)=g(b), hence it belongs to the top-left locus; the inclusion j yields the unique lift. Smoothness under the stated transversality is supplied by F1 and the transverse-fibre-product supplier. No orientation sign or extra intersection claim is asserted by the figure.

diagram_math_checks.proof: The original proof steps 1.1–3.1 are byte-preserved; the square illustrates only their existing coincidence-set identification.
